newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-BALLESTEROS AND LANGER HIT TROUBLE IN HAMBURG.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BALLESTEROS AND LANGER HIT TROUBLE IN HAMBURG.

text.p: Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros slumped 17 shots off the lead to miss the cut in the European Tournament Players' Championship on Friday, then said he was taking next week off.
That means Ballesteros, who pulled out of last weekend's PGA Championship at Wentworth with his recurring back injury, will miss the European Grand Prix in England.

Ballesteros has perennial back problems and one of his expected Cup lynch pins at Valderrama in September, Bernhard Langer, also missed the cut and then had to go to hospital with agonising back pain.
The German was subsequently found to be suffering a muscle spasm, a tournament official said.
Langer struggled to a second-round 76, three-over-par in total, as England's Van Phillips became the new leader by one shot.

The German had nearly missed the Players' Championship because of injuring a finger at Wentworth, where Ballesteros had to withdraw after a 76 in the first round of the PGA, his back so bad he could not stoop to pick up his ball.

However, after double-bogeying his last hole here by going into water to run up a seven-over-par 79 and total 12-over for the two rounds, Ballesteros was more worried about his ailing confidence than his bad back.
"After losing the ball there was no motivation left for me," said the Spaniard. "It's very clear. I will not be playing next week.

"My back is not too bad but I have no confidence. I haven't been able to play and then I've missed cuts, so everything has worked against me. The rhythm is not there, the concentration is just not there either and nor is my competitive instinct."

Ballesteros did not make it clear how long he is prepared to take off from the European Tour but he definitely will seek no further help from the Munich doctor who has treated his compatriot Jose Maria Olazabal so successfully.
"I don't know my schedule but there is going to be no more treatment from the doctor in Munich," he added. "This guy doesn't help my condition. I'm very happy for Jose Maria but he is no help to me."
It was Ballesteros's seventh missed cut in nine European Tour starts. He also missed the cut in the U.S Masters and does not qualify for the U.S. Open.

Phillips, the English player who wears a tie because of a clothing contract, took advantage of late slips by compatriot Barry Lane, who had established a three-stroke lead before dropping four shots in the last four holes.
A four-under-par 68 took Phillips to 139 -- one ahead of Spanish Ryder Cup prospect Miguel Martin, who shot 71, and Italian Emanuele Canonica, who carded 70.
Overnight leader Paul Broadhurst lost ground, going back into the pack on level-par after a 76.
